Commentary.Commentary: So that ends our coverage of the fourth Test between India and England at Wankhede stadium in Mumbai. It was a high voltage contest and the home side have further stamped their authority to win the series. The fifth Test will be a dead rubber but England would look to fight back and play for pride. Join us on 16th December for the final Test at 0930 IST. Till then, goodbye and take care!

INDIA SKIPPER AND MAN OF THE MATCH, VIRAT KOHLI - Mentions that it is a very special feeling to win the series. Adds that when he was taking a victory lap, he had a chat with Ashwin, that last time they were playing England here and lost the game mentally and on the field. Adds that they were mentally strong this time around and after they got a 231-run lead, the opposition was deflated. Adds that their batsmen adjusted well to the bounce on this track. Mentions that Murali Vijay was not quite going well in the series but adjusted beautifully to play a champion knock. Jayant Yadav was very very special and played a terrific knock. Adds that they were 2-0 up and he wanted to seal the series here itself. States that the intent helped him to capitalize on his innings. Mentions that when they got close to 400 they took control. Adds that going 3-0 up will allow them to really express themselves in the Chennai Test. Feels that the batsmen needed to apply themselves on this track and even the bowlers. Adds that they had an advantage as England had a spinner less. Opines that Ashwin is out there to win the man of the match award whenever he comes out to play and even the man of the series. Mentions that the batsmen play second fiddle to his bowling performances and he has been superb with the bat too. Adds that he is a very intelligent guy and he is delighted to have him in the team. Mentions that the English side played high risk shots and they are not very confident in their defense. Feels that this has been the difference between the two sides and the Indian batsmen have enjoyed their defense. Mentions that probably the change in mindset has done the trick.

ENGLAND SKIPPER ALASTAIR COOK - Feels that 400 was a pretty good score on this wicket but also mentions that they had an opportunity to get 450-plus. Adds that they had a chance as India were 300-6 but Virat Kohli played a terrific knock and Jayant Yadav played really well too. Opines that they couldn't win the key moments. Mentions that in hindsight, it was a wrong decision to go for the fourth seamer but their spin options are limited. Mentions that they will look at the bowling composition going forward. Feels that they have had their chances but haven't been good enough to get over the line. Feels that bowling a lot of overs makes the spinners get tired. States that even Ashwin gets tired when he bowls a lot of overs. Also mentions that they scored over 600 runs in this game. Adds that they batted well than the previous games but couldn't bowl out India under 400. Feels that Virat Kohli is in incredible form. Adds that he is one of the best batsmen of this generation.

The hosts then came in really well with the ball as they had England struggling at 49/3 by tea on day 4. Root and Bairstow stuck it out in between for some time but England lost the plot with the former's dismissal. India finished the day in style by reducing England to 182/6 with a wicket off the very last ball of the day. It was always going to be an uphill task for them from there on and they crumbled under pressure this morning.

India got their act right as they posted a huge total on the board in reply. Vijay was the one who started off the act in style. Kohli came in on the third day of the Test match and kept going for his third double century - all of which have come this year while Vijay also got to his hundred. They looked crippling for a moment when they lost their middle order in quick succession. However, Jayant came in and stuck it out with Kohli to strike a 241-run partnership. The former also got to his maiden Test ton as India managed to take a really good lead of 231 runs.

England would have been happy with their batting in the first innings where they were shown the path by the debutant Jennings who started off with a ton. Moeen Ali and Buttler also chipped in with vital fifties. The spin duo got all the quota of wickets where Ashwin got 6 for 112 and Jadeja managed to notch four on the other hand.

India have taken an unassailable lead of 3-0 in the five-match Test Series. They have finished off the final day in just more than half an hour of play. Ashwin and Jadeja continued from where they stopped yesterday as the off spinner took the remaining wickets today. Bairstow the only fighter who was well set, was sent back really quickly today and that opened the floodgates.
Virat Kohli is leading his troops for a victory lap around the Wankhede stadium. The crowd is really loud and is up on its feet cheering them.

Pitch Report - Sunil Gavaskar feels that consistency with the areas for the bowlers is key on this pitch. He also adds that the Indian bowlers have been far more consistent than the visitors. Opines that the pitch has detoriated really and batting on this track would be really tough.
Weather Report - It is a really bright and sunny day here in Mumbai. The chances of rain here seems really bleak.

Welcome to the final day of the fourth Test match between India and England. The tourists will have to bat out of their skins to take this game deep. Buttler and Bairstow are the only two frontline batsmen left in their ranks, they have a tough task ahead. Indians will be itching to come out there and finish the match as soon as possible. Just 4 wickets left for England and a deficit of 49 runs, can the visitors put their strings together and make life difficult for the Indians? Join us in a while as live action is not far away.
Day 5, Session 1...

With the likes of Buttler, Bairstow at the crease, England will hope they can wipe out the deficit quickly and put some sort of a score on board to try and put the pressure back on India. The hosts on the other hand, will aim to get the last four wickets quickly and push for an innings win. Will it happen though? Or do we have another twist in the tale? Do join us for all the action on Day 5 at 0930 IST. Until then, it's goodbye and take care.

The Indians will be happy as they batted really well earlier in the day to take a lead of 231 runs. Kohli and Jayant Yadav played the Englishmen out of the game with their partnership of 241 runs. The Indians came out really hard with the ball as they rattled out the top order in 13.2 overs of the second session but the lower order has stuck in again. It seems really tough for the English batsmen now to play through the final day as they have already lost 6 wickets and still trail by 49 runs.

Phew! What a day of Test cricket! England started off really well in the third session of the day where they started attacking the Indian spinners. Root and Bairstow really scored at a brisk pace which made the Indian spinners think. Root, who was toying with the bowlers, using his feet to find the gaps, putting pressure on the bowlers to change their lengths. It was Jayant Yadav who trapped him in front of the stumps and then England lost the plot a bit. Bairstow played through the session while Stokes gave him a brief company and Ball,who came in as a nightwatchman was out in the final over of the day.

Welcome back for the final session of play. England are trailing India by 182 runs and are up against it. Joe Root is joined by JONNY BAIRSTOW at the crease. Jadeja to complete his over. Here we go...
DAY 4... SESSION 3...

Jadeja got Cook and Moeen Ali out in quick succession. Root is still out there and will hope to stage a fightback of sorts, will he get support though since the ball is spinning a mile already. English middle order again has a tough job to do. Join us in a while for live action.

A really good session for the Indians as they came in really hard with the bat and scored 52 runs in no time. Jayant Yadav got his maiden Test Hundred in just his third Test. The Indians were really charged up when they came out to bowl. Bhuvneshwar rattled out Jennings on a golden duck just on the second delivery of the third innings. Root and Cook kept the Indians quiet for some period till Virat brought in the spinners.

OUT! Cook had played one through the same area and got away with it, Ali is not that lucky. Jadeja bowls it outside off, the ball turns in sharply with some extra bounce, Ali gets across and looks to clip it through. The ball flies quickly to Murali Vijay at leg slip who takes a sharp catch diving to his right. The Indian players mob Vijay who just stands in awe. He waits for a while before celebrating the wicket, a perfect session for India. They have a big wicket, Jadeja leads the team off the field. England are three down, still trail India by 182 runs. That's also TEA, DAY 4!
Floated outside off, Ali comes forward to defend it.
Root lunges forward and defends it back down the wicket.
FOUR! Top shot! Outside off, Root comes down, takes it on the full and drives it through extra cover for a boundary.

Floated outside off, comes in a touch, Root looks to defend but seems to have missed it. Parthiv Patel comes from behind and appeals for a catch after collecting the ball. There is a loud appeal for a catch. They go for a review more in desperation. Root was all smiles when India took the review. Replays confirm there was no bat there. They check for the lbw but it was spinning down the leg side.
India have asked for a review for a catch against Root.
Root comes forward and turns it towards mid on.

Fires it on off, Ali keeps it out towards mid on from his crease.
MOEEN ALI is the new man in.

OUT! COOK HAS TO DEPART! 100 Test wicket for Jadeja! Pitched outside off and that was turning into the stumps. Cook tries to flick it across the line on the on side but fails to find contact and the ball hits the pads. A loud appeal is made by Jadeja and the fielders around the batsman. The umpire thinks about it and raises the finger. Cook was quick to ask for a review. The reviews show that the bowl was pitched outside off, the impact was on line and the ball was hitting the leg stump. All three reds and the decision stands. Both the openers are now in the pavilion.
Cook is given out lbw but he goes for a review. That looked very close. It looked more like a tactical review.

FOUR! Nice timing! Landed on off, Cook clips it through mid-wicket. Rahul looks to give it a chase but the ball races away to the fence for a boundary.
Flatter on the pads, Cook looks to clip but cannot beat the fielder at short leg.
Cook leans across and works it through mid on for a single.
Root top edges his pull through square leg for a single.

DRAMA! Floated outside off, Root comes down to defend but is hit on his pads. The ball lobs towards short leg who takes the catch and appeals. He also has a shy at the stumps at the striker's end but Root got back in as he missed. There was no bat there despite the appeal.
Cook drives this one towards Rahul at extra cover who fumbles and allows a single. That is his second misfield.
Landed outside off, Root sweeps it through backward square leg for a single.
Floated outside off, Root comes down and clips it towards short mid-wicket who fumbles but no harm done.

FOUR! Did it carry? Yes but not a drop but a chance gone! Floated on middle and leg, Cook shuffles across and clips it just wide of the diving Murali Vijay at leg gully for a boundary to fine leg. That was a genuine chance there! He should have been at leg slip there.
Edged! Root looks to clip it through mid-wicket but gets a leading edge through covers for a single.

OUT! WHAT-A-BALL! In-swinging from outside off, Jennings tries to clip it on the on side through his pads but is unable to find his bat anywhere near the ball. The ball just zipped after pitching and hits on his pads. A loud appeal by the Indians and Bhuvi is rewarded for that delivery. Jennings has a chat with Cook but the latter denies to review it. The reviews show that it was in line and was clipping the leg stump. They have lost their first wicket. Jennings has to depart without troubling the scorecards for a duck.
